overview: The First Order Transporter is a atmospheric assault lander whose service history spans First Order (34 ABY–35 ABY). A heavily armoured troop carrier deployed during the attack on Takodana and the siege of Crait. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~4,000 units, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the First Order Transporter during the political tensions that defined First Order (34 ABY–35 ABY). Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a atmospheric assault lander, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the First Order Transporter entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. A heavily armoured troop carrier deployed during the attack on Takodana and the siege of Crait. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~4,000 units diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the atmospheric assault lander could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the First Order Transporter symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The First Order Transporter illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its atmospheric assault lander layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~4,000 units hulls served during First Order (34 ABY–35 ABY), making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the First Order Transporter remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
